content.user_title: Deploy Docusaurus Sites to GitHub Pages
content.value_statement: Deploying Docusaurus to GitHub Pages can fail when configuration, builds, or workflows are misaligned. This skill guides validation, GitHub Actions setup, and deployment checks.
actual_capabilities: Checks Docusaurus project structure, config files, sidebars, and dependencies.
Guides GitHub Pages url, baseUrl, organizationName, and projectName settings.
Provides local validation steps for dependency install, type checking, build, and serve.
Includes a GitHub Actions workflow template for Pages deployment.
Explains troubleshooting for 404 errors, broken links, workflow failures, and build errors.
Defines performance and content quality gates before publishing.
limitations: Does not host the site or authenticate with GitHub for the user.
Requires user-approved repository changes and GitHub push access.
Assumes an npm-based Docusaurus project and GitHub Pages target.
Workflow paths may need edits for monorepos or nonstandard directories.

use_cases.title: Launch a documentation site
use_cases.description: Prepare a Docusaurus project for first-time GitHub Pages deployment with correct config and workflow settings.

use_cases.title: Validate before publishing
use_cases.description: Run local checks for type errors, build failures, link issues, and content readiness before pushing changes.

use_cases.title: Repair deployment failures
use_cases.description: Diagnose GitHub Actions, Pages settings, baseUrl, and broken link problems after a failed release.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a new deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use docusaurus-deployer to inspect my Docusaurus project and list the GitHub Pages settings I must configure.

prompt_templates.title: Validate before publishing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use docusaurus-deployer to guide local validation for my site and report any blockers before I push.

prompt_templates.title: Create the workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use docusaurus-deployer to adapt the bundled GitHub Pages workflow for my repository layout and Node version.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a failed deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use docusaurus-deployer to review my config, workflow logs, and deployed URL symptoms, then propose fixes.

output_examples.input: Validate a Docusaurus site before GitHub Pages deployment.
output: A readiness checklist covering config values, dependency install, type checking, production build, local serving, and link checks.
A short blocker list with the exact settings or files that need attention before publishing.

output_examples.input: Set up GitHub Actions for a Docusaurus site in a subdirectory.
output_examples.output: A workflow adaptation plan that names the working directory, Node version, cache path, build output path, and Pages permissions.

output_examples.input: Fix a deployed site that returns 404 pages.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting sequence for baseUrl, repository name, Pages source, deployment history, and build artifact contents.

best_practices: Confirm url and baseUrl match the deployment type before building.
Run local type checking and production build before pushing changes.
Review workflow permissions and working-directory paths before enabling Pages.
anti_patterns: Pushing documentation changes before the local build succeeds.
Using hardcoded production URLs for internal documentation links.
Copying the sample workflow without adjusting repository paths.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy the site automatically?
faq.answer: It guides the deployment workflow and provides setup steps. The user must approve repository changes and pushes.

faq.question: Which hosting target does it support?
faq.answer: It focuses on GitHub Pages deployments for Docusaurus sites.

faq.question: Can it handle a Docusaurus site in a subdirectory?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow guidance includes working-directory and artifact path adjustments.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub secrets?
faq.answer: Most Pages deployments use GitHub Actions permissions and the built-in GitHub token. Extra secrets depend on the project.

faq.question: What should I check before pushing?
faq.answer: Check configuration values, type checking, production build output, local serving, links, assets, and workflow paths.

faq.question: Can it troubleshoot 404 errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers baseUrl, repository naming, Pages source settings, deployment history, and build artifacts.
